summary: Yuen Ren Chao specialized in linguistics and sinology. He studied at Tsinghua, Cornell, and Harvard, later holding posts at Cornell (circa 1919–1920), Harvard (circa 1921–1924), Tsinghua (circa 1925–1929), and the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1947–1963).
Yuexia was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He founded Huayan University and served as a teacher there.

Yuguang Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and completed his PhD at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1965 to 1974. He later served as president (学長) of Taisho University from circa 2011 to 2013.
Yui Chi Lau worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Ying-Kuang Chu, founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society, and taught Shek-Wing Tam.

Yui Suzuki works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. Suzuki studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and the University of Vienna, and held posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, and Soka University.

Yuichi Shionoya was a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He studied at Nagoya University (circa 1949–1953) and Hitotsubashi University (circa 1953–1958), and later held a post at Nagoya University from circa 1964 to 1968.

Yuishin Ito was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University, later holding posts at Bukkyo University, Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen, Shōjōke-in Temple, and Chion-in Temple.

Yujiro Motora worked in philosophy and other fields. After studying at Johns Hopkins University in 1885, he held posts at Tokyo University of Education (circa 1888–1898) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1888–1912).

Yujun Endo worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Taisho University, including associate professor (attested 1991) and professor emeritus (attested 2014), and served as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani works in Buddhist studies. In 2015, she was attested as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Ryukoku University and Hanazono University.
Yukari Kimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Kenyu Mitomo and is attested in 2026 holding a post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Yukei Matsunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Koyasan University, Tohoku University, and Kyushu University, and held posts as director at Koyasan University (1983) and at Shuchiin University (circa 1999–2004).

Yuki Kyogoku works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. A doctoral student at the University of Leipzig (attested 2026), Kyogoku worked as an associate engineer at Accenture (2013–2014) and a research associate at the University of Leipzig (2018).

Yuki Sasaki works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Sasaki holds posts as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yuki Shibuya is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Shibuya was a project research fellow at the University of Tokyo in 2014 and earned a Ph.D. there between 2016 and 2018.
Yuki Takatsukasa is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015). Takatsukasa later served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Asayama held a professorship at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and served as an overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).
Yukihiko Matsumura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Matsumura studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and held a post there as a specialist researcher (attested 2026).
